account: Today I reviewed my appointments and attended the east-bank mill grain inspection. The mill stall held 76 hay bales for sale at two emeralds each. I have not established any shortage or delivery difficulty. The unusual news is repeated talk among townsfolk of a 'bridge or port change at bakery.' Their accounts place the baker, freight, innkeeper, builder and neighbour there, though not every account names everyone. One report also says the innkeeper carried a sack of bread. I have heard these reports from townsfolk, not from the participants, and have not seen the reported change myself. I therefore cannot yet say what changed, who arranged it, or what it is for. It might concern transport or deliveries, but that remains speculation; a sack of bread alone does not establish anything improper. I asked the secretary to find someone with a firsthand account. She reports no correspondence and has confirmed that the neighbour expects tea at fifteen and needs no preparations for our ordinary eighteen o'clock town hall meeting. I have no evidence linking that meeting to the bakery reports. I am now home after the scheduled noon lunch period and should return to the office for council letters at thirteen, with tea at fifteen and office hours at sixteen-thirty still to follow.
